title: Meta Pixel & Standard Events
objectives: Understand what the Meta Pixel does on a website
Identify Meta's standard events: ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase, and Lead
Verify active tracking using the free Meta Pixel Helper Chrome extension

blocks.text: The Pixel is Meta's eyes and ears on your website! Without it, Ads Manager is flying blind.
The Meta Pixel is a snippet of JavaScript code placed in the header of your website. It reports every action visitors take back to Meta.

rows: User opens a product or service page
User submits an inquiry or quote form

blocks.title: The Shop Assistant Bell
blocks.text: Every time a customer picks up a product, adds it to their basket, or walks to the cash counter, a little bell rings in Meta's headquarters. That bell is a Standard Event!
Install the free 'Meta Pixel Helper' extension on Google Chrome. It glows green and shows a checkmark when your Pixel events fire properly.
Always pass the currency parameter as 'INR' and value with real purchase prices so Meta can accurately report your ROAS.

quiz.q: Which standard event should fire when an online shopper completes payment on the order confirmation screen?
quiz.explain: The 'Purchase' event must only fire on the final Thank You / Confirmation page when money is received.

quiz.q: What free tool do media buyers use on Google Chrome to test if pixel events are firing correctly on any website?
quiz.explain: Meta Pixel Helper is the official Chrome extension used to inspect and troubleshoot active pixel tags.

quiz.q: True or False: If you run a 'Sales' campaign without a pixel installed, Meta can still automatically calculate your ROAS.
quiz.explain: False! Without the Pixel or CAPI, Meta has zero visibility into purchases and cannot report or optimize for ROAS.

quiz.q: Place the standard e-commerce events in chronological order from landing to checkout.
quiz.explain: A user first views content, adds to cart, starts checkout, and completes the purchase.

recap: Meta Pixel reports website user actions (events) back to the ad auction.
Key events: ViewContent → AddToCart → InitiateCheckout → Purchase / Lead. Verify using Pixel Helper.
